ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: On the left side of the figure is a current source labeled 1 A, with the arrow pointing upward. The upper end of the current source passes through a 1 Ω resistor, then reaches the middle network composed of two 4 Ω resistors connected in parallel up and down, and then connects to the right-side node. Between the right-side node and the lower common node there are two vertical 2 Ω resistors connected in parallel. The voltage U is marked on the far right, with the positive terminal on top and the negative terminal on bottom, so U is the voltage across these two right-side 2 Ω parallel branches. Then reason: According to the connection relationship in the figure, the two right-side 2 Ω resistors are connected in parallel, and their equivalent resistance is 2 Ω || 2 Ω = 1 Ω. The left-side 1 A current source forces the current in the entire series path to be 1 A, so the total current flowing into the right-side equivalent parallel network is 1 A. Therefore the voltage across this parallel network is U = I R = 1 A × 1 Ω = 1 V.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use parallel-resistance formulas: 4 Ω || 4 Ω = 2 Ω and 2 Ω || 2 Ω = 1 Ω. In a series path driven by an ideal 1 A current source, the same total current enters the final parallel equivalent. The voltage across a parallel network equals the current into its equivalent resistance times that equivalent resistance, V = IR.

raw_record.original_question: In the circuit shown in the figure, what is the value of the voltage \(U\)?
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: On the left side of the figure is a current source labeled 1 A, with the arrow pointing upward. The upper end of the current source passes through a 1 Ω resistor, then reaches the middle network composed of two 4 Ω resistors connected in parallel up and down, and then connects to the right-side node. Between the right-side node and the lower common node there are two vertical 2 Ω resistors connected in parallel. The voltage U is marked on the far right, with the positive terminal on top and the negative terminal on bottom, so U is the voltage across these two right-side 2 Ω parallel branches.

Then reason: According to the connection relationship in the figure, the two right-side 2 Ω resistors are connected in parallel, and their equivalent resistance is 2 Ω || 2 Ω = 1 Ω. The left-side 1 A current source forces the current in the entire series path to be 1 A, so the total current flowing into the right-side equivalent parallel network is 1 A. Therefore the voltage across this parallel network is U = I R = 1 A × 1 Ω = 1 V.
